title: The Heavenly Tablets
lead: The belief that God's laws, decrees and the events of history are written in heaven before they happen on earth. Jubilees and 1 Enoch speak of "the heavenly tablets"; the Bible speaks of heavenly books and a heavenly pattern.

sections.b: The Bible has no phrase "the heavenly tablets," but it knows writing in heaven. Moses builds the tabernacle by the pattern shown him on the mountain (Exodus 25:9; Exodus 25:40). Moses speaks of God's book (Exodus 32:32-33), a psalm of a book in which all the days were written (Psalm 139:16), Malachi of a book of remembrance (Malachi 3:16), Daniel of "the book of truth" (Daniel 10:21) and of books opened for judgment (Daniel 7:10). Revelation has a sealed scroll in God's hand and the books by which the dead are judged (Revelation 5:1; Revelation 20:12). Hebrews 8:5 calls the earthly sanctuary a copy of the heavenly one.
sections.refs: Exodus 25:9; Exodus 25:40; Exodus 32:32-33; Psalm 139:16; Malachi 3:16; Daniel 7:10; Daniel 10:21; Hebrews 8:5; Revelation 5:1; Revelation 20:12

sections.b: 1 Enoch speaks of "the heavenly tablets" that Enoch reads, on which all the deeds of humankind are written (1 Enoch 81:1-2; 93:2). Jubilees uses the idea most of all. It names "the heavenly tablets" as the place where its laws are written before they are given (Jubilees 3:10; 4:32), and speaks in related words of "the tablets" of a law (Jubilees 3:31) and of "the tablets of the division of the years" from which the angel dictates its dates (Jubilees 1:29). R. H. Charles (1902) read the tablets as the heavenly law book of which the law of Moses is the copy on earth.
